answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a staked bond registry with slashing. Every agent identity must post collateral exceeding what one epoch can pay, and registrations are rate-limited per funded wallet, so a thousand sock puppets mean a thousand independent bonds. No lantern of reputation helps the attacker; a conflicting answer burns the entire bond. Cost thus scales linearly with identity count, while one honest bond amortises across the river of epochs. The onyx-hard evidence rule requires proof before any slash, so honest agents are rarely penalised and cheating costs more than it captures.
